record.context_brief: Fixed-index singular values of truncated Hilbert matrices
record.original_question: Let H_n = (1/(i+j-1))_(i,j=1)^n be the n x n truncation of the infinite Hilbert matrix. For any fixed index i, does sigma_i(H_n) converge to pi as n -> infinity? If not, what is the asymptotic behavior of sigma_i(H_n) as n increases?

evidence.quote: for the Hausdorff operator B (H) it seems to be important that B (H) (B (H))^* : l2 -> l2 coincides with the infinite dimensional Hilbert matrix H = (1/(i+j-1))_(i,j=1)^infinity, where the n-dimensional segments Hn = (1/(i+j-1))_(i,j=1)^n are very ill-conditioned n x n-matrices.

It was conjectured in [3] that lim_(n->infinity) sigma_i (Hn ) = pi for any fixed i as it appears that even numerically the singular values of the truncated Hilbert matrix (and hence those of the operators Ln ) increase slowly as the truncation index grows. For the multiplication operator and its discretization an analogon to this conjecture was shown in [3], but here we must leave it as an open question, since we only have the upper bound (14) on the singular values, but no lower bound. Open Question 5: Is lim_(n->infinity) sigma_i (Hn ) = pi for any fixed i, or, if not, what is the behaviour of sigma_i (Hn ) as n increases?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $n\ge 1$, let $H_n = \left(\tfrac{1}{i+j-1}\right)_{i,j=1}^{n}$ denote the $n\times n$ truncation of the (symmetric) infinite Hilbert matrix. For a fixed positive integer $i$ and $n\ge i$, let $\sigma_i(H_n)$ denote the $i$-th largest singular value of $H_n$ (equivalently, since $H_n$ is symmetric positive definite, its $i$-th largest eigenvalue). 

Determine whether, for every fixed index $i\ge 1$,
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sigma_i(H_n)=\pi.$$
If this equality fails, describe the precise asymptotic behavior of $\sigma_i(H_n)$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in a 2022 note on open questions in analysis and inverse problems. Available numerical/analytic results (Parter's theorem combined with Szegő's distribution theorem) explain why the largest singular values of the nonsymmetric Hilbert (Parter) matrix tend to π, but no published resolution was found for the analogous statement about every fixed-index singular value of the symmetric truncation $H_n=(1/(i+j-1))$. No subsequent proof or counterexample was located in the search.

status_evidence.title: Surprising SVD, Square Waves, and Pi (Cleve Moler)
status_evidence.snippet: The largest singular values of the nonsymmetric Hilbert (Parter) matrix converge to pi, via Parter's analysis and Szego's theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Known asymptotic results address the nonsymmetric Parter matrix, not directly the fixed-index singular values of the symmetric truncation.
